answer: Land-title binding: each agent's operator proves ownership or a registered lease of one land parcel. Validators query the public land registry, mail a one-time code to the titled address, and store a salted hash of the parcel number, so one parcel backs one earning identity. Splitting a farm into forty agents still shows one title near the yarrow field; each extra identity needs another recorded parcel with its own deed fees and yearly property tax. Limit: wealthy operators at the zenith of the market can buy many lots, and renters in a gale-swept city may be shut out.
